issues.description: Blocking read after first byte removes timeout and process-exit safety net, can hang forever.
issues.detail: Once O_NONBLOCK is dropped, the inner while-True loop has no poll timeout and no check_process_exited. If the writer wedges after one byte, or a grandchild inherits the write fd and never closes it, the reader hangs indefinitely. The minimal fix is to do one final blocking drain on detected exit, not a permanent mode flip.

issues.description: fcntl O_NONBLOCK flip is unguarded, unrestored, and unchecked for failure.
issues.detail: F_SETFL mutates the fd's flags as a side effect with no try/finally restoration. If the inner read raises, or any other holder of the fd relies on O_NONBLOCK, behavior changes silently. Wrap the flip in try/finally to restore original flags, or do not flip modes at all and keep polling with a sane timeout.

issues.description: No regression test reproducing the >64KB truncation bug.
issues.detail: Correctness rests entirely on a POSIX argument in the commit message. Add a test with a subprocess that writes >64KB and exits immediately, run in a loop, that fails without the patch and passes with it. Without a test, this bug returns the next time someone touches the function.

issues.description: Function complects wait-for-first-byte and drain-to-EOF with a mid-loop mode switch.
issues.detail: Two distinct phases (non-blocking poll until first byte, then blocking drain) are braided into one loop with a break that exits the outer loop from inside the inner one. Decompose into wait_for_first_byte() and drain_to_eof(fd) so each concern is one concept and the control flow is legible.

issues.description: Loop invariant and termination assumptions are not stated in the source.
issues.detail: The hybrid strategy depends on unstated preconditions: exactly one writer, writer will close, no inherited write fds in grandchildren. POSIX guarantees EOF only when all write ends close. Write the invariant and termination argument into the code, not the PR description, so the next reader can verify the proof.

issues.description: Dead control flow after rewrite: BlockingIOError branch, else: pass, and has_blocking_error guard.
issues.detail: The else: pass branch, the except BlockingIOError: pass branch, and the outer while-not-has_blocking_error guard are no longer meaningfully reachable or mutable after the inner break. Either delete them, or annotate them as pre-first-byte-only. Stale explanatory comments next to no-op code confuse the next reader.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the diagnosis is sound and the POSIX blocking-read argument is essentially correct, but the patch is the wrong shape. By dropping O_NONBLOCK permanently after the first byte, it deletes the subprocess-exit and timeout safety nets that motivated the original poll loop, leaving the reader hangable if the writer wedges or a grandchild inherits the write fd. The fcntl flip is also unguarded and unrestored, and the rewrite leaves dead branches whose meaning is no longer stated. NEEDS-WORK: shrink to a minimal final-drain on detected exit, restore fd flags in try/finally, state the termination invariant in the source, and add a regression test for the >64KB truncation.
